items.caption: This oracle-bone-style form shows a frontal human figure with a vertical body, arms extending to either side, and separated legs. It fits the analysis of 大 as a human figure, though the precise pose and original sense remain interpretations.
items.alt: Black oracle-bone-style glyph with a long upright body, outstretched arms, and two separated legs.
items.selection_reason: The candidate gives a useful early-style example for the human-figure analysis. Its visible pose also makes clear why “arms outstretched” is a shape description, not proof of the graph’s original meaning.

items.caption: This Western Zhou bronze-style redraw retains a frontal human-like form, with a tall central body, lateral arms, and legs below. A bronze inscription cited in the specialist account uses 大 opposite 小, but this redraw alone does not establish that usage or a precise date.
items.alt: Black bronze-script-style glyph with a tall central stroke, broad arms, and two curved legs.
items.selection_reason: It adds a visually distinct bronze-script form and connects to the reported bronze use meaning “big”; the inscription evidence is cited separately from the image’s appearance.

items.caption: This Shuowen seal-style redraw has a balanced human-like outline: a central upright stroke, arms slanting outward, and two long legs. It illustrates a dictionary-script form without establishing a stroke-by-stroke path from earlier forms.
items.alt: Black seal-script-style glyph with a central upright, sloping arms, and two long legs.
items.selection_reason: It provides a useful comparison with the oracle-bone- and bronze-style redraws while avoiding an unsupported claim that the shapes document a precise sequence of changes.

limitations.text: These are modern redrawings in named script styles, not photographs of ancient objects. The adult-human interpretation is supported by specialist analysis, but the visible pose does not by itself establish the graph’s original meaning; one local account’s “outstretched arms” explanation conflicts with the analysis of arms hanging down.

The images permit broad comparison of script styles, but they do not establish a precise chronology of graphic changes or the earliest dated use. The adult-to-big semantic development is a proposed analysis, and its intermediate stages are not documented here.
